title: Sealed lumeri-engine dispatcher
summary: The only engine entrypoint offered to the sandbox. Dispatch chooses a fixed subcommand, reads one JSON object from its request file, and writes a report to stdout with an exit status. Per-command JSON shapes belong to engine.gemia.

replaceability.why: The sealed dispatcher, execution broker or sandbox is trusted integrity machinery.

reach.notes: Trusted Runtime seam, not an additional grant to a creator Luc.

operations.name: main
operations.notes: No fixed operation deadline is enforced; the enclosing authorized sandbox profile supplies its execution ceiling. argv includes executable name. Queries require three argv items and artifact commands four. Exit 0 can carry a domain refusal; 2 is usage/input, 3 unavailable engine or unexpected execution error, 4 declared render/artifact mismatch. CLI itself has no execution_id replay or atomic Project commit; only scratch outputs are permitted by its Runtime sandbox.

invariants.text: The dispatcher imports only fixed engine entrypoints; a request cannot name arbitrary Python code.

break: An unhandled exception, invalid output, or failed declared artifact check.
failure.notes: The original reports failure today. The self-Luc run gate and original fallback are requirements for a future replacement, not a promise this seam already implements.

conformance.notes: Only contract/schema checking exists here; no replacement conformance runner.

known_deviations.text: A nonzero exit and a JSON refusal are different contracts. sandbox.run currently raises on nonzero and keeps stderr while discarding stdout from that exception path, so caption options printed to stdout can be lost.
